findings.title: Missing React key on GrafanaRuleListItem in list rendering
findings.body: In FilterViewResults, the 'grafana' switch branch renders <GrafanaRuleListItem> without the `key` prop (the old <GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} ...> had it, and every other branch still passes key). Since these items are rendered inside rules.map() and the list grows via infinite scroll, React cannot stably identify items; adding/removing rules can reuse component state (open dropdown menus, silence drawer state, redirect state) across different rules and can cause incorrect DOM reuse. The key must be restored, e.g. key={key}.

findings.title: Silence drawer never opens for Grafana rules without rulerRule (list view)
findings.body: The 'Silence notifications' menu item is now shown based on grafanaPromRuleAbilities when only a promRule is available (AlertRuleMenu line 126 checks canSilence, which ORs the prom-based ability). However, the drawer rendering is still gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, which is false when no RulerRuleDTO was passed. In the alert list view (where the ruler API is no longer called and only promRule is supplied), clicking 'Silence notifications' sets showSilenceDrawer=true but SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is never rendered — the action silently does nothing. The drawer needs to be constructible from the prom rule / GrafanaPromRuleDTO as well.

findings.title: Pause menu item requires rulerRule, so pause is unavailable in the list view
findings.body: canPause is computed as an OR of ruler-based and prom-based abilities, so in the alert list view (promRule only, no rulerRule) the menu can report pause as supported/allowed. But the actual menu item is additionally gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana'`, which is false when rulerRule is undefined. Result: users with permission see no way to pause Grafana-managed rules from the list view, a functional regression versus the previous list implementation. MenuItemPauseRule needs a prom-rule/GrafanaPromRuleDTO variant.

findings.title: Delete menu item requires rulerRule, so delete is unavailable in the list view
findings.body: canDelete now ORs in the prom-based ability so the menu logic considers delete permitted when only promRule is available, but the Delete item rendering is gated on `canDelete && rulerRule` and the click handler `handleDelete(rulerRule, ...)` requires a RulerRuleDTO. In the alert list view, where the ruler API is no longer fetched, users with delete permission will never see the Delete action for Grafana rules — a regression from the previous behavior where each rule's ruler data was loaded. handleDelete should be adapted to work from the rule identifier/prom rule.

findings.title: Creating/deleting rule states no longer rendered and tests deleted without replacement
findings.body: Removing the ruler group query means rules that exist in the Ruler but not yet in Prometheus (newly created, previously shown with a 'Creating' state) are never displayed, and rules deleted from the Ruler but still present in Prometheus (previously shown as non-actionable 'Deleting' items) now render as fully normal, actionable list items. The tests covering both behaviors ('should render rule with url and creating state when only ruler rule exists', 'should render delete rule operation list item when only prom rule exists') and the matchRules unit tests were deleted rather than replaced. If eventual-consistency handling is intentionally dropped, the PR should state so; otherwise rules will appear stale/actionable during the propagation window.

findings.title: isProvisionedPromRule depends on `provenance` field that the Prometheus API may not return
findings.body: The client-side change adds `provenance?: string` to GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase and uses `isProvisionedPromRule` (checking promRule.provenance) to decide immutability (edit/delete/pause) for Grafana rules in the list view. If the backend /api/v1/rules (Grafana Prometheus endpoint) does not actually include provenance in its response, provisioned (file-based) Grafana rules will be treated as mutable and users will be shown Edit/Delete/Pause actions that will fail on save. This should be verified against the API contract (or covered by an MSW mock that omits provenance) before merging.

findings.title: Silence ability for GrafanaPromRule ignores loading state of folder/permissions
findings.body: In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, [AlertRuleAction.Silence] is [silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]. Unlike the ruler-based useCanSilence (which returns [false,false] while folder is loading or missing), canSilenceInFolder evaluates immediately: while the folder is still loading, hasFolderSilencePermission is false, so a user whose only silence permission is the folder-scoped AlertingSilenceCreate will see the Silence item flicker (hidden, then appear) — and worse, useFolderPermissions returns {} for a rule whose folder cannot be resolved, so such rules rely solely on the global permission. Consider gating on folder loading for consistency.

findings.title: Each Grafana list item now triggers per-rule folder fetches via hooks
findings.body: GrafanaRuleListItem renders RuleActionsButtons which calls useGrafanaPromRuleAbility, and AlertRuleMenu calls useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities; each useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities invocation runs useFolder(folderUid) and useGetGrafanaAlertingConfigurationStatusQuery. With the old ruler-based flow these were partially memoized via useAllAlertRuleAbilities; now every rule in a large list (e.g. 80+ rules) issues hook-driven folder lookups (once per unique folder, but the ability memo/object is per-rule) — verify that the folder query is deduplicated by RTKQ caching and that the double evaluation (ruler hook + prom hook both running in AlertRuleMenu/RuleActionsButtons for every rule) doesn't measurably regress list rendering.
